application_review: PROGRESS. Prior audit rechecked before saving the baseline; old proof hashes preserved.
The weighted square identity expands the actual sum of subgroup Haar averages and applies the previously proved pair-energy identity term by term.
Cauchy-Schwarz with the unit-bounded original function proves the first-order energy inequality. This part even allows signed subgroup coefficients.
An elementary variance proof gives Jensen for weighted squares. Applying it to actual nonnegative normalized cell weights produces the weighted-cell energy inequality.

For normalized nonnegative subgroup weights, the square-root identity for actual first-order Gowers values and their unit bounds yield the quartic Bessel inequality. No projection or orthogonality assumption is introduced.

Six new theorems are individually kernel audited. The quartic result is first-order only; it is not a substitute for the arbitrary-order Tao-Ziegler theorem required by the master short-cube argument.
